chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed and then gave the salam in two rak'ahs. Those behind him asked him, 'O Messenger of Allah, has something new happened in the prayer?' He said, 'What is that?' They said, 'You have only prayed two rak'ahs.' He said, 'Is that so, O Dha al-Yadayn?' And he was called Dha al-Shimalayn. He said, 'Yes.' So he completed his prayer and made it four, and said, 'Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the One who caused me to forget out of mercy for the Ummah. Do you not see that if a man had done this, he would have been mocked?' Then it was said to him, 'Your prayer is not accepted,' on the day that happened. He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had established a precedent, and it became a model, and he prostrated two prostrations for the sake of the speech.'

key_terms.ذَا الْيَدَيْنِ: Possessor of the two hands (a title for the Prophet)
key_terms.رَحْمَةً لِلْأُمَّةِ: Out of mercy for the community
key_terms.لِمَكَانِ الْكَلاَمِ: For the sake of the speech/talking

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Prophet's prayer being accepted when he forgot and prayed only two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet's two-rak'ah prayer, where he was reminded by Abu Bakr (known as *Dhā al-Yadayn*) and completed the prayer, establishing the precedent for *Sujud al-Nasī'* (prostrations of forgetfulness). The narration highlights the theological principle that the Imam's forgetfulness is a divine mercy (*rahmah*) for the Ummah, distinguishing it from the error of an ordinary individual who might be criticized. It further clarifies that the Prophet's pause for conversation was the specific cause of his forgetfulness, reinforcing the validity of this practice as a lasting Sunnah.
